title: Location loot table
description: A loot table for one location type, per docs/12-resources.md: 'A loot table declares location type, resource weights, tier weights, and quantity ranges.' A map's loot entry names one of these by its location, and SimBoot.place_loot rolls it. Adding a location type -- a school, a marina, a police station -- is one entry here plus map tagging, with no code change. NOTE: the content validator is shallow (top-level types and unexpected top-level keys only) and does not recurse into `entries` or the range objects; check_loot.gd is the gate that does, and it is the reason a wrong key inside a nested block cannot sit here unnoticed the way one did in item.wrap.cloth's armor block.

location.description: The location type, matching the map loot entry's `table`. The enum is docs/12's five scavenging locations; Milestone 2 authors three of them.

danger.description: docs/12's risk gradient, which is the difficulty curve. Declared here so the table and its danger cannot drift apart; nothing reads it yet -- the director will.

rolls.description: How many picks this site yields, inclusive. Not how many items: a pick can be a stack.

tierWeights.description: Relative weights over the item tiers this location yields. Keys must be SimItems.TIERS ids; a location that never yields a tier simply omits it. This replaces SimItems.roll_tier for placed loot, which is how a military cache comes out better than a kitchen drawer.

entries.description: The weighted pool. Weights are relative within this table only.

count.description: Quantity range for a stackable base, inclusive. Omitted means exactly one. SimItems clamps to the base's own stack limit.
